result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.astar_path_length()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find the length of a shortest path with the A* search algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L46379-L46433){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.astar_path_length( source, target, heuristic=None, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![A* path length](/assets/graphs/astar-path-length.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Four towns A, B, C, D joined by roads: A–B 4, B–D 4, A–C 2 and C–D 7. From A (outlined) to D (outlined) the route through C starts cheaper but totals 9, so A* returns the route through B, drawn in the accent color, with length 4 + 4 = 8.0." width="100%"} Runs the same search as `astar_path()` and returns the total length of the path found: the number of edges on an unweighted graph, or the sum of edge weights on a weighted one. See `astar_path()` for how the heuristic speeds up the search. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The endpoints, as IDs or labels. [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The endpoints, as IDs or labels. [heuristic]{.doc-parameter-name}[=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op}[None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional function `heuristic(node_id, target_id) -> float` that never overestimates the remaining distance. If `None` (default), every estimate is `0`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int, float, or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The path length (`int` hops when unweighted), or `None` if the target cannot be reached. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist or a weight is negative. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Identical to `astar_path()`; see there. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#99191a3b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec roads = ec.Graph(weighted=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) roads.add_edges([("A", "B", 4.0), ("B", "D", 4.0), ("A", "C", 2.0), ("C", "D", 7.0)]) roads.astar_path_length("A", "D") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 8.0 ``` ::: :::
